Hi Samantha — glad these were useful. Responses below and attached artifacts.

1) Break-glass workflow
- Workflow: Support engineer submits break-glass request -> Security approver notified -> Approver must approve via console + 2FA -> Temporary elevation granted for a configurable window (default 1 hour)
- Audit trail: every request/approval logged with timestamp, approver id, justification, and auto-expire flag. Logs are immutable and exportable.
- Alerts: optional Slack/Email alerting to your SecOps channel on every break-glass event.

2) Support access scoping
- Support sessions are session-scoped by default; exports require a separate, auditable export action limited to Admin or Security roles.
- Session recording: we can turn on session capture (metadata + transcript) with consent flags; recordings are stored in your pinned region and subject to your retention policy.

3) Retention
- Retention is configurable per-tenant and per-log-type. We support the 7-year retention you mentioned; note that longer retention increases storage costs — we can provide cost estimates.

4) Compliance artifacts
- Attached: SOC2-Excerpt-Redwood.pdf (redacted) and a short RBAC overview PDF. We also have a pen-test summary available under NDA — happy to share if you send your standard NDA.

Attached files:
- Redwood_RBAC_BreakGlass_Overview.pdf
- SOC2-Excerpt-Redwood.pdf
- RBAC-role-mapping.xlsx (template)

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the role-mapping template and send back by EOD Wed (13 Jan) so we can map to our role set and show a demo.
- Tech deep-dive: propose Thu 14 Jan 10:00 PT (30–45m) with Dev (dev.patel@redwoodinference.com) to walk logs, session recordings, and the approval flow.
- I’ll also add a quick cost estimate for 7-year retention to the HubSpot deal record (FT-2027-0143).

Let me know if Thu 14 at 10:00 PT works and if you need the NDA — I can send a standard one.
